patterns.name: Locus Is Not Its Carrier
patterns.invariant: A Carrier is a replaceable execution embodiment; no property of the locus is defined in terms of the thread, core or process currently carrying it.
patterns.prior_art: M:N scheduling; green threads; BEAM processes are not OS threads. The tree's statement is a standing rule (computedriven/receipts/R7-OPEN.md §0), not a measured result — the measured fact is carrier-multiplexing.
patterns.headline: A locus is not the thread running it; the thread is a replaceable embodiment.
patterns.explanatory: Everything a locus is — its seal, its state, its admissible transitions — is defined without reference to the carrier currently executing it. Swap the thread for a core, the core for a machine, and nothing the locus is has changed. This is a standing rule in ComputeDriven, and the measured fact beside it is Carrier Multiplexing.
patterns.technical: R7-OPEN §0, permanent standing rules from R2.1 and the R6 freeze: 'A Locus is not a thread; a Carrier is a replaceable embodiment.' There is no THREAD in the progress model's §4. A locus's context (KERNELLET-R1: admission + finality warden + possession) is the locus's; possession is a field that says which carrier, if any, holds it now.
patterns.problem: Most runtimes define the unit of computation as the thing that executes: a thread, a process, a container. Identity then dies with the carrier: a restart is a death, a migration is a copy, and 'the same agent' has to be re-asserted by convention rather than established by a seal.
patterns.forces: It is convenient to store a locus's state on its thread's stack. It is fast. It also makes every carrier replacement a serialization problem and every serialization a chance to make a Replica. The rule costs a level of indirection on every access to the context and buys carrier independence as a property rather than a promise.
patterns.construction: Give every locus a seal (Identity Is a Seal) and a context that lives outside any carrier. Model possession as a field with three states — vacant, attached, suspended — on the context, not as the carrier's opinion. Make carrier replacement a floor command that moves possession, and forbid every read of the context from asking which carrier holds it.

allowed: replacing the carrier while possession moves atomically
running the same locus on a thread today and a machine tomorrow
suspending possession with no carrier at all (Dormant But Alive)
forbidden: deriving identity, authority or state from the carrier
serializing a context by copying and calling the copy the locus
treating loss of a carrier as loss of the locus

patterns.consequences: The system stops asking 'is the thread alive?' and starts asking 'is the locus established?'. That is the whole shift of Part I, and it is why the agency definition on this site says models and harnesses are components a locus reasons through, not identity criteria.
patterns.analogy: A chess game is not the board it is played on. Move the pieces to a new board, or play by post, and it is the same game at the same position; the board never had an opinion about which game it was.
patterns.applicability: Any system that must survive its own restarts, migrations or hardware: agent runtimes, durable workflows, the T&R shell's windows, FPLA elements. It is a rule to adopt at design time; retrofitting it means finding every place a thread-local was used as identity.

patterns.name: Identity Is a Seal
patterns.invariant: The identity of a semantic artifact is the hash of its canonical form, computed identically on every host; two artifacts with different futures have different seals.
patterns.prior_art: Merkle 1979; Nix store paths; Unison identifies every definition by the hash of its syntax tree. 'birth key' appears once in WRL/HANDOFF_D8_PATH_B.md; the invariant's wording is the book's.

patterns.name: Continuity Through Reconstruction
patterns.invariant: A locus continues across a replacement iff a minimal causally established support set sufficient for each declared capability is retained; reconstruction from durable facts is continuity, not creation.
patterns.prior_art: Atkinson & Morrison, orthogonal persistence (persistence independence); Erlang code change; distillation as successor. Never write in the present perfect: stage 5 (Inheritance) has never been reached.

patterns.name: Refusing Join
patterns.invariant: Composition of two independently produced assemblies either yields a composite that satisfies the compose laws or is refused naming the field that made it impossible; refusal is a valid outcome, not a failure.

witness.rung_source: STACK_COMPLETION.md corrections §1: 101 compose laws, 2000 trials, derived totals

counterexample.note: v0.4 named the marker narrow-into-ANY-refused, which is CD2's FAILURE string (a refusal that must NOT happen). A marker proves the file mentions a string, not that the string is a refusal — P2 finding; the page runs CD1 live.

patterns.prior_art: Monoid laws (associativity, identity). FACTORY_REVIEW_BUNDLE.md cites 'the 2026 λA literature, Theorem 5.7' from page copy only — NOT SEARCHED for the paper.
patterns.headline: A join that cannot be made is refused, and the refusal names the field.
patterns.explanatory: Two assemblies built in ignorance of each other are brought to a join. Either the composite satisfies every compose law the algebra states, or the join returns the annihilator and says which contract field made it impossible. Nothing is coerced, defaulted or repaired on the way through. A refusal is a first-class outcome of composition, not an error path around it.
patterns.technical: For bricks a, b with declared contracts, composePipe(a, b) is either an admitted composite or 0̲ (ZERO, annihilated). An UNDECLARED contract field is not a wildcard: undeclared |> narrow ⇒ 0̲ (CD1). An explicit ANY is directional: a narrow producer composes into an ANY consumer, an ANY producer does not compose into a narrow consumer (CD2). & does not launder undeclaredness into a declared interface (CD3). The identities none() and idBrick() DECLARE '*' so the identity laws survive without the fix degenerating into refuse-everything (CD2/CD4). 101 enforced compose laws, 2000 trials each, totals derived by the suite.
patterns.problem: Systems built from independently produced parts need a place where parts meet. The conventional join coerces: an absent interface defaults to the most permissive one, a mismatched type is widened, a missing field is repaired. On 2026-08-22 exactly that bug was found in this algebra — Brick() defaulted an absent contract field to '*', so an assembly that declared no interface at all received the most permissive interface in the algebra, and every hand-off passed a check that had nothing to check. Five falsifiers were written against the unfixed code and all five failed.
patterns.forces: Refusing is cheap to implement and expensive to live with: every refusal is work someone must redo, so the pressure is always toward 'just compose it'. The identity laws must still hold, or the fix degenerates into refuse-everything (CD2 and CD4a exist for that). MISSING ≠ UNIVERSAL has to have content in both directions. And a refusal must NAME what it refused, or the producer cannot repair its side — a silent 0̲ is only marginally better than a silent coercion.
patterns.construction: Represent contracts as terms with an explicit UNDECLARED kind distinct from ANY. Normalize before comparing (norm). Make composition total: it always returns a brick, and the annihilator ZERO is a brick with annihilated === true. Preserve the identities by having none() and idBrick() declare '*'. State the narrowed domain as its own law (CD4b) rather than leaving it implicit. Derive every printed total from the suite; hand-typed totals drifted three times before this rule.

allowed: re-associating a chain of joins (|> is a phase-graded monoid)
commuting operands of & (a commutative idempotent monoid)
declaring a contract explicitly where one was absent — this can only turn a refusal into a composite, never the reverse
forbidden: defaulting an absent contract field to '*' or any other value
widening a type to make a join succeed
repairing evidence on the way through a join (VALUE laws: defaults complete absence, never repair)
treating the annihilator as an exception or a crash

patterns.consequences: Composition becomes something a receiver can check, not something it must trust. The cost is that an under-declared assembly is unusable until it declares, which is the point. Refusal ≠ failure: the three-valued outcome vocabulary (APPLIED · REFUSED · INDETERMINATE) in three-valued-outcome is this principle for interventions.
patterns.analogy: Customs at a border between two factories. A crate with a declared manifest that matches the receiving line goes through. A crate with no manifest is not waved through as 'could be anything' — it is turned back with a slip that says which field was missing. The slip is the product of that transaction, and it is worth more than a crate that was let through on a guess.
patterns.applicability: Use it wherever two things built separately must meet: assemblies at a factory join, capability bricks in a governance ladder, records from two verifiers, agents handing work to agents. Do not use it where the join is the identity operation on one thing — an identity must DECLARE '*', or the pattern degenerates into refuse-everything.

syntax.label: How a refusal carries its reason — the annihilator is a brick

takeaways.text: A join is a check on declared contracts; a refusal is a returned value that names the field.
0̲ is a Brick with annihilated: true and a refusal string — composition is total, and the failure case is data.
MISSING ≠ UNIVERSAL: an absent contract field normalizes to {kind:'undeclared'}, never to '*'. The identity elements declare '*' explicitly so the identity laws survive.

The two laws a refusing join must keep — associativity and identity — are the monoid laws; the factory page notes the λA literature derived the same pair independently (paper not yet located: prior_art says so).
This is not an argument: 101 laws × 2000 trials ran in your browser above, on the same bytes CI runs.

patterns.name: Refusable Divergence
patterns.invariant: An implementation divergence between two verifiers of the same artifact is refused by name rather than passing silently: no flags, no prose, only claims a receiver recomputes.

witness.rung_source: STACK_COMPLETION.md:73; two verifiers in two languages (WRL js, TRVM Forge python)

patterns.prior_art: Content addressing; Nix; 'refused by BOTH sides' is WRL/PACKET_README.md:109's wording; 'agree on the name of every refusal' is STACK_COMPLETION.md:73's and is not verified by this build. WRL/HANDOFF_D8_PATH_B.md:1424 warns that two refusals can both be drift.
patterns.headline: A divergence between two implementations is refused by name, not passed in silence.
patterns.explanatory: Put only claims on the wire — no flags, no prose. Every receiver recomputes the claims from the bytes. Two verifiers in two languages then either agree or refuse, and a refusal names what it refused. A negative corpus of tampered records is part of the artifact, so 'refuses' is something you can run.
patterns.technical: WRL §D8.19, the projection on the wire. deriveRuntimeProjection makes the V1→V2 downgrade in-band. Conformance: 924 checks passing today (STACK_COMPLETION recorded 890 in August). Negative corpus: 15 tampered records stored as final bytes, refused by both verifiers; a consumer must check the wire differs from its base before trusting a refusal, and whether refusal codes are normative is an open question the corpus states itself.
patterns.problem: Two implementations of one format drift. The usual defence is a version flag and a prose note, and both are things a receiver is asked to believe. When the implementations disagree, the disagreement passes silently and shows up later as data that two systems read differently.
patterns.forces: Recomputing claims costs a receiver work it could skip by trusting a flag. A negative corpus is only evidence if each tamper actually differs from its base — a recipe that matches nothing is a fixture that passes while asserting nothing. And two refusals can both be drift: agreement on a refusal is weaker than agreement on the bytes.
patterns.construction: Seal the artifact (Meaning Is a Hash). Put the recomputable claims on the wire and nothing else. Keep a negative corpus as final bytes beside the positive vectors. Run two independent verifiers and require both to refuse every tamper; report code disagreement separately from the refusal.

allowed: adding a verifier in a third language
adding a tamper to the corpus (with its base named)
downgrading a projection in-band, so the receiver sees the downgrade as a claim
forbidden: a flag or a prose note that a receiver is asked to trust
a fixture that is an edit recipe rather than final bytes
collapsing two refusals into one because they agree

patterns.consequences: Interoperability becomes a property with a witness: two repos, two languages, one corpus. The remaining honesty is in the corpus's own note — code normativity is open — and in WRL's handoff warning that two implementations can both have drifted.
patterns.analogy: Two auditors who each recompute the total from the receipts rather than reading the number at the bottom of the page. If the page lies, both say so, and each says which line.
patterns.applicability: Any format with more than one implementation: wire protocols, certificate formats, manifests, the projection vectors between WRL and TRVM Forge. Not for a single implementation that can only agree with itself.

Tampers are stored as final bytes, not edit recipes, because a recipe that matches nothing passes while asserting nothing.
Content addressing (Merkle, Nix) makes the seal; the contribution here is the refusal name on the wire and the shared negative corpus across two implementations.

patterns.name: Progress Over Utilization
patterns.invariant: System health is measured by admitted semantic transitions per unit cost, never by carrier busyness; a Carrier may be fully busy while the loci it carries make no progress.

witness.rung_source: R7-EXECUTED.md header: battery receipt R7-BATTERY-20260905T172007Z from a clean tree; 'the busiest Carrier is the one making the least progress'

patterns.prior_art: Erlang reductions as the scheduling unit; Little's law; the utilization-vs-throughput distinction in queueing theory. computedriven/docs/progress-model.md is a MODEL (its header: 'never a measurement') and is not this witness.
patterns.headline: Measure admitted transitions per cost, never carrier busyness.
patterns.explanatory: Utilization is a fact about carriers. Progress is a fact about loci. A carrier can be fully busy relocating loci for fairness while nothing is admitted. R7's first executed pass found exactly that: the busiest carrier was the one making the least progress.
patterns.technical: Unit: instructions per admitted transition (the receipts' unit). The progress floor profile (commit 684aad3) and the multiplexer battery (cff8a3d) compare a progress arm against fair arms; the fair arms spend most of their commands relocating. computedriven/docs/progress-model.md defines the terms and says of itself: every numeral is a definition or a prediction, never a measurement.
patterns.problem: Every dashboard shows CPU %. Schedulers optimize fairness among runnable threads. Both measure the carrier. A system can run at 100 % and admit nothing, and the metrics will call it healthy.
patterns.forces: Progress needs a definition before it can be counted — an admitted semantic transition — and a definition is a commitment the model document has to make ahead of the receipt. Fairness is a real value; starving a locus forever is not progress either. The pattern does not say ignore fairness; it says do not mistake it for the goal.
patterns.construction: Define the unit (admitted transition), instrument it at the floor, and report it per cost. Keep utilization as a diagnostic, never as the health signal. Run a fair arm beside the progress arm so the comparison is measured, not argued.

allowed: lowering utilization while raising admitted transitions
re-placing loci to where progress is possible (Progress-Aware Placement)
forbidden: scheduling work that admits nothing to keep a carrier busy (Busywork Scheduling)
quoting a model document's number as a measurement

patterns.consequences: The health question moves from the carrier to the loci, which is where the semantics are. It also makes the next pattern possible: placement can be chosen for progress only once progress is what is measured.
patterns.analogy: A kitchen where every cook is moving constantly and no plates leave the pass. The manager who counts moving cooks sees a busy kitchen; the one who counts plates sees the problem.
patterns.applicability: Schedulers, agent runtimes, benchmark harnesses, anything with a dashboard. Especially where a fairness policy already exists and has never been measured against what it admitted.

syntax.label: Where the fair arms spent their commands

takeaways.text: Equal utilization, unequal progress — the meters that matter are the lower ones.
The receipt's title is the finding: the busiest Carrier is the one making the least progress.
Queueing theory separated utilization from throughput long ago; Erlang counts reductions, not busy schedulers. The pattern is the old distinction applied to loci.
The witness is a receipt with instruction counts; the model document beside it is a prediction and is not cited as evidence.

patterns.name: Dormant But Alive
patterns.invariant: A locus with no Carrier and pending mailbox depth is fully live: its admissibility and future transitions are defined, and readiness changes without executing a floor command.

witness.rung_source: an OPEN record: the admission rule is specified, the battery is R7.1's

patterns.prior_art: BEAM processes; durable execution (Temporal, Restate); delimited continuations.
patterns.headline: A locus that consumes no compute can be fully live.
patterns.explanatory: Liveness is a semantic property: does the locus have a defined state and admissible next transitions? Placement is a resource property: does a carrier hold it right now? A locus can be live and unplaced. Its mailbox accumulates events that change its readiness, and none of them executes anything until a carrier takes it.
patterns.technical: R7.1 admission: a per-Locus mailbox of depth M in the multiplexer. An event changes readiness but executes no floor command by itself (FPLA design A restates the same separation). Placement moves possession from vacant to attached; the pending work is exactly the mailbox contents.
patterns.problem: Runtimes conflate 'idle' with 'done' and 'unscheduled' with 'dead'. A garbage collector, a supervisor or a human reads an empty carrier and concludes there is nothing to do, while a locus with a full mailbox waits above the floor.
patterns.forces: A dormant locus costs memory for its context and its mailbox, so the depth bound M is real: past it, the multiplexer must refuse admission rather than grow. The temptation is to let the scheduler treat the mailbox as advisory. The pattern says it is an admission rule.
patterns.construction: Separate readiness from execution: an event arriving updates a ready-set and nothing else. Make placement an explicit floor command. Keep the mailbox on the locus's context, bounded by M, and refuse the (M+1)th event at admission with a named refusal rather than dropping it silently.

allowed: a locus holding no carrier for any length of time
placing a dormant locus on any available carrier
forbidden: executing a floor command as a side effect of an event's arrival
inferring 'nothing to do' from 'no carrier busy' (False Quiescence)

patterns.consequences: 'Is the system quiet?' stops being answerable from the carriers. That is the gap Proven Quiescence names — and that pattern is still PROPOSED, which this page says plainly.
patterns.analogy: A doctor on call. Not in the building, not being paid by the hour, and still on the roster with a pager that changes what happens next. The hospital being quiet says nothing about the pager.
patterns.applicability: Actor systems, agent runtimes with many more agents than cores, durable-execution engines, and any system that must answer 'is there pending work?' honestly.

syntax.label: The admission rule (R7.1-OPEN — an OPEN record; specified, its battery not yet run)

takeaways.text: Readiness changed three times while nothing executed; placement is what made the pending work run.
Mailbox depth M is an admission rule: the (M+1)th event is refused, not queued forever.
BEAM processes and durable-execution engines embody this; continuations are the older form.
STATED, not witnessed: the source is an OPEN record, and the label on this page derives from that.

patterns.name: Carrier Multiplexing
patterns.invariant: A population of loci larger than a floor's slot count is carried by rotating loci through slots; the slot is not the unit of identity and no locus is lost by not currently holding one.

witness.rung_source: R7-EXECUTED.md:101 'Eight slots multiplex 64 Loci at 97.4 B'

patterns.prior_art: M:N threading; Go's scheduler; Erlang schedulers.
patterns.headline: More loci than slots, carried by rotation, and no locus is lost by not holding one.
patterns.explanatory: A floor has a fixed number of slots. A population of loci may be far larger. Multiplexing rotates loci through slots; the slot is a temporary embodiment and the locus's identity, state and admissible transitions are unchanged by leaving it. R7 measured eight slots carrying sixty-four loci.
patterns.technical: Per-Locus mailbox of depth M in the multiplexer (R7.1 admission); a slot holds one Locus Core Context (309 B production profile, KERNELLET-R1); rotation is a floor command, not a copy. Instruction counts per admitted transition are the receipt's unit.
patterns.problem: Threads are expensive and identity is cheap. A system that gives every locus its own thread, core or process runs out of carriers long before it runs out of things worth being; and a system that then says 'the locus IS the thread' has to kill loci to free carriers.
patterns.forces: Rotation costs commands, and a fair rotation spends most of them relocating. The per-locus mailbox bounds what a waiting locus can accumulate, and that bound is an admission rule the multiplexer must enforce, not a scheduler hint. The picture is easy; the receipt is what says whether the rotation left any progress behind.
patterns.construction: Give the floor N slots and the population K > N loci. Keep every locus's context outside the slot (the 309-byte context is the locus's, not the slot's). Rotate by floor command; never copy a context to move it. Measure instructions per admitted transition, not slot occupancy.

allowed: growing the population without growing the floor
changing which slot a locus is rotated into
adding a slot (the population is unchanged)
forbidden: copying a context to 'move' a locus — that is Replica Theater
deriving any locus property from its current slot
declaring completion because every slot is empty

patterns.consequences: Capacity becomes a question about admitted transitions per cost rather than about carrier count. The trap is that the utilization meters look wonderful while nothing is admitted; Progress Over Utilization is the measuring pattern this one needs beside it.
patterns.analogy: A hotel with eight beds and sixty-four guests on a night shift roster. A guest who is not in a bed has not ceased to exist, and the hotel does not photocopy guests to move them.
patterns.applicability: Any floor whose population exceeds its carriers: agent runtimes, actor systems, cooperative schedulers, the FPLA's array elements. Not for systems where the carrier is the identity by design (a physical device with one owner).

patterns.name: Proven Quiescence
patterns.invariant: A system is quiescent only when a sweep establishes that no locus has admissible pending work; silence of the currently observed carriers is not completion.

patterns.name: Three-Valued Outcome
patterns.invariant: Every attempted intervention resolves to exactly one of APPLIED, REFUSED, INDETERMINATE; INDETERMINATE is a fact about an attempt and is never rewritten.
patterns.prior_art: Two Generals; at-least-once vs at-most-once delivery; Lamport's 'happened before'. Witness lives in super/ (referenced, not copied); the document's §0 refutes the PREDECESSOR round's settle-in-place design.

patterns.name: Orthogonal Persistence
patterns.invariant: Whether a locus's state is in cache, RAM, disk or a remote node is an implementation choice below its semantic level; code is identical for short-lived and long-lived state.
patterns.prior_art: Atkinson & Morrison's term: type orthogonality, persistence by reachability, persistence independence (PS-algol, Napier88; VLDB J. 4, 1995). studbook is at the spec rung; nothing here implements it.

patterns.name: Three Sizes of World
patterns.invariant: WORLD (the machine, 10 GB–10 TB), WORLD VERSION (a content-addressed root, KB) and WRL GRAPH (the semantic layer inside, KB–MB) are three sizes with three names; no field is called current_head — a head is always qualified.
patterns.prior_art: Git's object/ref/worktree split is the same three-way distinction. Frozen vocabulary in CLOUD_V1.md §2 because WORLD_SIZE.md §11 mistook 0.21 % for the whole.

patterns.invariant: The semantics of a WRL world is its SemanticArtifactID; a change of meaning is a change of hash and a preserved hash is a preserved meaning on every host, forever.

patterns.name: Exact Replay
patterns.invariant: A run of a sealed world is a film that replays byte-identically; any divergence on replay is a divergence of the world, not of the player.
patterns.prior_art: Deterministic replay; event sourcing; rr. TRVM film replay — not verified by this build; no receipt stating a fidelity percentage was located (v0.2 review finding 7).

patterns.name: Cross-Machine Skill Replay
patterns.invariant: A skill taught on machine A replays on machine B with the declared fidelity; the InteractionTrace is the unit of transfer.

witness.rung_source: a receipt CARD on the homepage; the run behind it was not opened by this build

patterns.prior_art: OS-011 Embodiment; record-and-replay in RPA. v0.1 conflated this with exact-replay.

patterns.name: Confidentiality Under Content Addressing
patterns.prior_art: OPEN BLOCKER (studbook §10): if the key is the hash of the content, knowing the content is knowing the key. Convergent encryption and its known leaks are the prior art. The book publishes the refusal, not a pattern.

patterns.name: Established, Not Known
patterns.prior_art: Byzantine observation: an observation can be stale, forged or partial; 'establish' names what survives that. STALE ≠ UNESTABLISHED (Super bot spec).

patterns.name: State Does Not Grant Authority
patterns.invariant: Admissible action = f(established state, explicit grant, policy, contracts), never f(established state) alone; a fact about a locus never constitutes a power.

counterexample.lint_allow: lint-allow:STATE_DOES_NOT_ISSUE_AUTHORITY — a lint counterexample must print the retired phrase to be one

patterns.prior_art: Object-capability discipline (Miller); 'fact about me ⇒ power is ambient authority with an extra step' (AGENCY.md §4). Under R7's criterion this may belong in the locus family.

patterns.name: Evidence Before Claim
patterns.invariant: A public proposition is admitted only with a named witness that exists; a claim whose witness is absent, whose antecedent is missing, or whose cell binding contradicts the table is refused.

witness.rung_source: runs over CLAIM_LEDGER.json (190 claims) and refuses; exit code is the verdict

patterns.prior_art: Toulmin's warrant/backing; Pollock defeaters; assurance cases (GSN). The phrase is absent from the tree; the mechanism (DOCTRINE.md rule 4 + the ledger) is not.

patterns.name: Refusal Gate
patterns.invariant: Below material sufficiency the page is not written and the reason is published; a check that can be satisfied by constructing its own argument is not a check.
patterns.prior_art: Fail-closed defaults; Popperian falsifiability as an admission rule. The Academy refusal log is MOCK (ACADEMY.md:79); alkeyword's refusal rule is the live instance.

patterns.name: Intervention Provenance
patterns.invariant: Every intervention on the world carries the identity of the Worker and generation that made it and the evidence it acted on; an intervention that cannot be attributed is not admissible.
patterns.prior_art: Audit logs; provenance (W3C PROV). Witness lives in super/; the honest half of the record is that the re-observation it depends on does not exist (Pty::winsize() has zero callers).

patterns.name: Descent Is Not Dependence
patterns.invariant: A lineage edge generates a candidate support set and establishes none; support for a capability requires ablation, intervention, runtime dependency or replacement replay, and provenance-only support is refused.

witness.rung_source: both refusals fire on the synthetic corpus; 0 observed capabilities

patterns.prior_art: Pearl's ladder of causation; ablation studies; Λ non-laundering (cell 44). Lint class PROVENANCE_AS_SUPPORT enforces the prose form.

patterns.name: Understanding Boundary
patterns.invariant: A locus distinguishes what exists, what it can observe, what it believes, what it understands, what it intends and what it may alter; a claim in one register is never promoted to another without evidence.
patterns.prior_art: Epistemic logic (Hintikka); the ladder's epistemic rung. Graphonomous Bot spec: 'a Bot knows its projection, not the world.'

anti_patterns.name: Carrier Identity
anti_patterns.problem: Treating a thing as the process, thread or container currently executing it.

anti_patterns.name: Location Leak
anti_patterns.problem: Encoding physical placement into identity when placement is not semantic.

anti_patterns.name: False Quiescence
anti_patterns.problem: Declaring completion because no currently observed worker has work.

anti_patterns.name: Invisible State
anti_patterns.problem: Allowing state that affects future behaviour to remain outside the shared observable.

anti_patterns.name: Ambient Authority
anti_patterns.problem: Granting access to an environment because some part of it needs one capability.
anti_patterns.paid_for: AGENCY.md §4 (the phrasing that walks into it); Miller 2003 is the term's source

anti_patterns.name: Replica Theater
anti_patterns.problem: Calling independent mutable copies 'the same thing'.
anti_patterns.paid_for: CLAUDE.md: the served box-and-box copy is a MANUAL COPY and nothing syncs it

anti_patterns.name: Busywork Scheduling
anti_patterns.problem: Maximizing resource utilization while semantic progress stalls.
anti_patterns.paid_for: computedriven/receipts/R7-EXECUTED.md title: the busiest Carrier makes the least progress

anti_patterns.name: Agent Omniscience
anti_patterns.problem: Letting an agent's claims exceed its evidence boundary.
anti_patterns.paid_for: AGENCY.md §6 (what is established vs a reading)

anti_patterns.name: A Number in Two Places
anti_patterns.problem: A count or definition typed where it is displayed instead of derived from its source; the two drift.
anti_patterns.paid_for: STACK_COMPLETION.md corrections §1 (law counts 129→116→118); UNBOXED_PATTERNS.md v0.1 (32 labels over 30 rows; 890 vs 924)

anti_patterns.name: Record Is Locus
anti_patterns.problem: Inferring that X is a locus because X carries the locus fields.
anti_patterns.paid_for: AGENCY.md §1 corollary; caught on review of the factory page

anti_patterns.name: Provenance as Support
anti_patterns.problem: Treating a lineage edge as causal support for a capability.

anti_patterns.name: The Quiet Correction
anti_patterns.problem: Fixing a published error without retracting it by name where it was published.
